answer: A new identity must first prove it holds a real stake, then the network publishes an atlas of every agent's behavioral fingerprint. Each epoch, an agent's answer acts as a beacon, broadcasting its persona signature to the whole economy. The network then maps those beacons against the atlas and looks for dense clusters, which are the natural shape of a sybil reef. To survive detection, an attacker has to grow a whole coral reef of beacons at once, each requiring real compute and real stake, so the marginal cost of each extra fake identity is high and the cluster stands out immediately.
